title: Supabase open-sources real-environment evaluations for coding agents
friendlyTitle: Supabase releases tests for AI agents that build real backend features
summary: Supabase released the benchmark and regression framework it uses to test Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode on tasks such as schema creation, Edge Function debugging and row-level security fixes. Scenarios run against containerised Supabase environments and combine deterministic checks with semantic grading.
friendlySummary: The open-source tests ask coding agents to build databases, fix functions and repair security rules in a working Supabase setup. The system checks whether the finished work actually behaves correctly.
whyItMatters: Teams can adapt the framework to measure whether agents complete realistic backend work instead of relying on generic coding scores. Supabase’s early findings also show that current documentation and well-triggered skills can correct outdated model habits, making evals useful for improving the surrounding developer experience.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Developers can use this approach to test an agent on real jobs before trusting it in production. The results can also show where better instructions or documentation are needed.
